narrative.intro: AMI Metals has obligations of $1.5B in FY2026 to date from federal contracts. AMI Metals received 9 awards so far this fiscal year, with an average award size of $164M. AMI Metals obligations are up 3016758.9% year over year. AMI Metals shows minimal activity in earlier years, with obligations of $9.8K in FY21, $165K in FY22, $109K in FY23, $346K in FY24, and $48.9K in FY25. AMI Metals receives the vast majority of FY2026 obligations from one buyer: the Department of Homeland Security obligated $1.5B. AMI Metals does limited work with the Department of Defense, which obligated $13.5K. AMI Metals largest market is Process, Physical Distribution, and Logistics Consulting Services, with $1.5B in obligations. AMI Metals also has activity in Other Support Activities for Air Transportation, with $13.5K in obligations. The current-year totals are partial, covering fiscal year to date rather than a full year.

sections.heading: Who are AMI Metals top federal buyers?
sections.body: The Department of Homeland Security obligated $1.5B to AMI Metals in FY2026 to date. The Department of Defense obligated $13.5K to AMI Metals in the same period. Those two agencies are the only buyers listed for FY2026 to date.

sections.heading: What markets and contract sizes drive AMI Metals Federal revenue?
sections.body: Process, Physical Distribution, and Logistics Consulting Services accounts for $1.5B of AMI Metals obligations in FY2026 to date. Other Support Activities for Air Transportation accounts for $13.5K. AMI Metals has 9 awards this fiscal year and an average award size of $164M.
